title: Marc Lamont Hill BLOWS Candance Owens MAGA Mind Over Racial Double Standards
description:
Candace Owens sits down with Marc Lamont Hill for one of the most direct conversations either of them has had about policing, protest, and what a social movement is actually supposed to accomplish. The two come from opposite ends of the political spectrum, and neither one softens their position to make the conversation easier. What follows is a long, unfiltered exchange that moves through character, statistics, movement history, and economics without ever settling into agreement.

The disagreement starts with a question that a lot of people found uncomfortable at the time and still argue about today: does a person's past change how we should judge the way law enforcement treated them? Candace argues that honesty about someone's history matters, that public mourning shouldn't rewrite a record, and that elevating the wrong figure sends a damaging message to young people watching. Marc pushes back on the entire premise, arguing that the relevance of a criminal record collapses the moment you ask whether the person was a victim of a homicide, and that rights which depend on personal virtue aren't rights at all. That single exchange sets the terms for everything that follows.

From there the conversation moves into data, and this is where it gets genuinely substantive.
